Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — Samir and I dug into the prototype and we like the latency profiles. Before we take this further with procurement we need two things from you: a) your hosted API rate card (baseline pricing, any volume bands), and b) a clear explanation of how streaming responses are metered. Specifically:

- If a client disconnects mid-stream, do you bill for the partial tokens that were generated and sent, or only for completed responses?
- If a client retries (the app reconnects to ask the same prompt again), is there an idempotency or grace policy to prevent double billing?
- Any special handling for long-lived streams (e.g., patient-monitoring sessions that can be open for minutes)?

We also want to understand what discounts look like for a 12-month committed contract (approx 1M tokens/month).

Could you share the rate card + short note on the streaming semantics? A PDF/Excel would be great.

Best,
Olivia Zhang
Head of Data & Analytics
Clarity Health

Hi Olivia — great to hear the demo went well. Attaching our standard Q1 rate card (PDF) and a short note below that addresses your three bullets.

Attachments: Redwood_RateCard_Q1_2026.pdf (pdf, 450KB)

Baseline hosted pricing (public):
- Text generation (standard models): $0.015 per 1k output tokens
- Chat / multi-turn (includes context handling): $0.020 per 1k output tokens
- Embeddings: $0.0008 per embedding (per request)

Streaming billing (summary):
- Tokens are billed when generated by the model and successfully emitted to the client socket. In practice this means tokens that reach the client are billable.
- If a client disconnects mid-stream and reconnects without an idempotency/session key, a re-generated stream may produce duplicate output and that duplicate generation is billable.
- We support idempotency/session tokens on the hosted API — if your client provides the same session id for a retry within a 15-second grace window we will attempt to resume or deduplicate generation and avoid double-billing.
- For long-lived streams, billing is continuous while the model generates tokens. We offer advice on batching and prefix-caching for long-lived monitoring sessions to reduce unit costs.

Discounts: for a 12-month committed volume ~1M tokens/month we typically start at a 12% committed-use discount off public rates; field negotiation may push to 15% depending on uplift (support/SLAs).

If it helps, we can propose a draft commercial term that includes a small incident credit for transient disconnects during trial/rollout. I’ll loop in Marissa (AE) and Rishi (finance) to confirm what we can offer for Clarity.

Thanks — attaching the PDF now.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

2) The 15s grace-window is promising. For our use case we expect occasional mobile disconnects that last 30–45s. Would you consider extending the grace window (or applying a one-time rollout credit) so we can test without worrying about initial overages?
3) For an agreed 12-month 15% discount, can you confirm whether streaming-specific mitigations (dedup on session id, credits for reconnects) are included in that commercial?

Samir and I discussed a proposal: 12-month term, 15% discount, and a one-time $5k goodwill credit to cover early-stage reconnect overages. If you can confirm yes/no quickly we’ll raise the PO.

Hannah / team — I discussed with finance ops. Proposed position:

- Commercial: We can accept a 12-month commitment at 15% off public rates for the stated volumes (1M tokens/mo) provided the deal has a standard payment cadence and a 30-day auto-renew opt-out window.
- Streaming semantics: Billing is for tokens generated and emitted. To reduce disputes, we will define in the SOW: "emitted tokens = tokens successfully sent to client socket at the TCP layer or acknowledged by the HTTP stream; buffered tokens not delivered are non-billable."
- Grace/credits: Approve a one-time $5,000 rollout credit limited to reconnects under 30s. After that cap is reached, standard billing applies. Credits are applied to the first invoice and are non-recurring.
- Product note: Prioom (Product) to confirm that extending the dedupe window from 15s -> 30s is safe for dedup behavior. If product can’t guarantee dedupe beyond 20s, we should keep 20s in the API doc and offer the 30s grace as a business exception only for this customer.

I’m attaching a suggested rate card worksheet (RWD_ratecard_clarity_v2.xlsx) with line items and a placeholder quote. If you want, we can include the credit and a short clause in the MSA addendum.
